verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes that the auxiliary supply must power sensors for standalone debugging rather than only the ESP32.
The client defines the 1A USB auxiliary regulator, complete 3.3V load, Schottky OR-ing, and standalone-programming activation behavior.
The client only reports an untested LED voltage specification; the source does not establish that the standalone USB rail must power the LEDs.
The source concerns GPIO control of the 5V LED rail and does not create a distinct change to the standalone USB 3.3V supply.
The source assigns LED power and logic translation to the 5V rail but does not change the standalone USB 3.3V supply state.
The client explicitly locates the USB-C programming port and standalone-operation LDO on the legacy main board.
The client unambiguously accepts INA3221 as the replacement for INA219, changing the identity of the current-monitor load powered by the complete 3.3V rail.
The client identifies an unresolved mismatch between the specified 1A standalone USB regulator and the schematic's 800mA device.
The client changes DCDC1 to 3.4V before the Schottky OR-ing drop so the shared system rail remains at 3.3V.
The client changes the SK6812 LEDs from 5V to the complete 3.3V rail, making them loads of the standalone USB supply.

value_updates.normal_operation_source: AXP2101 DCDC1 programmed to 3.4V via I2C before the integrated-board Schottky OR-ing drop

verdicts.decision_note: The single-board redesign moves the auxiliary regulator and OR-ing circuit onto the integrated board and makes the old condition requiring an absent power board obsolete; unchanged source-selection semantics are omitted.
The source addresses connector-placement flexibility and does not independently establish the USB regulator's board location; that topology change is already represented by message 750.
